Also, a panel of chairman in Lok Sabha and a panel of Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha is appointed. Secretary-General is the head of the Secretariat of both the Houses. He is a permanent oﬃ cer appointed by the Speaker of the House. The Parliament (4) *Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was introduced in 1954 and came into force on 15 June, 1955. *All the punishable oﬀ ences under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are cognizable and triable summarily. *The trials of crime under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is done by First Class Judicial Magistrate and in case of Metropolis it is done by Metropolitan Magistrate. *Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 was brought into force from 26 October, 2006. *Criminal Tribes Act was ﬁ rstly enacted in 1871. *The Scheduled Castes and The Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is applicable in India since 30 January 1990. To implement the objectives of The Scheduled Castes and The Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, the central government has the power to make law. *Section 18 of The Scheduled Castes and The Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 prohibits anticipatory bail to the accused. *According to Rule 7 of this Act, an oﬀ ence committed under this act shall be investigated by a police oﬃ cer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police. *Under section 14 of this act the state Government for the purpose of providing speedy trial is empowered to constitute a court of session to be a special court for each district to try the oﬀ ence under SC & ST Act. *Hindu Marriage Act, Hindu Succession Act and The Commission of SATI (Prevention) Act were enforced in 1955, 1956 and 1987 respectively. *Right to Information came fully into force on 12 October 2005. Right to Information is a legal right. According to Supreme Court it is a fundamental right also. The use of Right to Information Act is to obtain information from public authority. *Namit sharma V/s Union of India case is related with Right to information Act 2005. The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan is an Indian political organization best known for its demand for the Right to information Act. Right to Information (Amendment) Act, 2019 removed the previous provision i.e., the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) and Information Commissioner (IC) at the Central and State level will hold oﬃ ce for a term of ﬁ ve year and substituted it by term as may be prescribed by the Central Government. *National Green Tribunal was established on 18 October, 2010, under National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. *The provision of the Panchayats (extension to scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 or PESA is a law enacted by the Government of India for ensuring self governance through traditional gram sabhas for people living in the Schedule Area of India. 1. In which year was Prevention of Food Adulteration Act ﬁ rst enacted? (a) 1951 (b) 1954 (c) 1964 (d) 1956 U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006 Ans. (b) The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 came into eﬀ ect on 1st June, 1955. 2. All oﬀ ences punishable under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are : (a) Cognizable and Non-bailable (b) Cognizable and Summarily Triable (c) Non-congnizable and Bailable (d) Non-cognizable and Compoundable M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2012 Ans. (b) According to Section 15 of Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 all the oﬀ ences punishable under the act are cognizable and summarily Triable. 3. Oﬀ ences are tried under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 by the Courts of (a) Sessions Court (b) Judicial Magistrate First Class (c) Judicial Magistrate Second Class (d) Chief Judicial Magistrate M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014 Ans. (b) The ﬁ rst class Judicial Magistrates have been empowered to hold special courts for the trial of oﬀ ences under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955. In Uttar Pradesh, in each district, the Courts of Chief Judicial Magistrates/ Judicial Magistrates have been designated as a Special Court for the trial of oﬀ ences under the Act. 4. Under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, All oﬀ ences are – (a) Cognizable (b) Bailable (c) Compoundable (d) Punishment with imprisonment and ﬁ ne both M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2013 Ans. Apart from it, this act provides for imprisonment as well as ﬁ ne to the oﬀ ender as a mode of punishment. Thus both option (A) and (D) are correct. questions.questionTextEn: When the court, under section 12 of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, shall presume that the oﬀ ence is committed on the ground of "untouchability"?
questions.questionTextHi: नागरिक अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1955 की धारा 12 के तहत अदालत कब यह मानेगी कि अपराध "अस्पृश्यता" के आधार पर किया गया है?
optionsEn: When it relates to member of Scheduled Castes only
When it relates to member of Scheduled Tribes only
When it relates to members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes both
optionsHi: जब यह केवल अनुसूचित जाति के सदस्य से संबंधित है
जब यह केवल अनुसूचित जनजाति के सदस्य से संबंधित है
जब यह अनुसूचित जाति और अनुसूचित जनजाति दोनों के सदस्यों से संबंधित हो
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Section 12 - Presumption by courts in certain cases: Where any act constituting an oﬀ ence under this act is committed in relation to a member of a scheduled caste, the court shall presume, unless the contrary is proved, that such act was committed on the ground of 'untouchability'.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) Section 12 - Presumption by courts in certain cases: Where any act constituting an oﬀ ence under this act is committed in relation to a member of a scheduled caste, the court shall presume, unless the contrary is proved, that such act was committed on the ground of 'untouchability'.

Its purpose was to help the process of land reforms in India

Women with two children get reduced entitlements. Select the correct answer using the code given below:

Hence statement (3) is correct. Maternity leave of 12 weeks to be availiable to mothers adopting a child below the age of three months from the date of adoption. Further, the provision of section 11A states that employer shall allow 4 visits a day to the creche by the women employee. Hence statement 2 is not correct.

Disaster Management Act, 2005 3. Enemy Property Act, 1968 4. Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes :
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से किसने लॉकडाउन के दौरान भारत सरकार द्वारा प्रयोग की गई असाधारण शक्तियों को कानूनी आधार दिया? 1. मानसिक स्वास्थ्य देखभाल अधिनियम, 2017 2. आपदा प्रबंधन अधिनियम, 2005 3. शत्रु संपत्ति अधिनियम, 1968 4. महामारी रोग अधिनियम, 1897 नीचे दिए गए कोड से सही उत्तर चुनें। कोड :
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). A 123-year-old law has come to the rescue of the government in its eﬀ ort to tackle the Covid-19 challenge. The decision aimed to ensure that all advisories of the Union Health Ministry and State governments on the COVID-19 crisis were enforced. Besides this, the government also invoked the Disaster Management Act, 2005 to enforce the 21-day nationwide lockdown that started at the midnight on 23 March, 2020. Thus, both Acts gavs legal basis to extraordinary Powers exercised by the Government of India during Lockdown.
